summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Translation synthesizes polypeptide chains from mRNA codons at the ribosome. Four sequential stages: (1) Aminoacylation / Charging of tRNA (ATP + Aminoacyl-tRNA Synthetase); (2) Initiation (small subunit binds mRNA, initiator tRNA occupies P-site); (3) Elongation (incoming aa-tRNA binds A-site, 23S/28S rRNA Peptidyl Transferase ribozyme catalyzes peptide bond, EF-G translocates ribosome); (4) Termination (Release factors bind stop codon).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
TRANSLATION CASCADE STAGES
                                       │
  1. AMINOACYLATION ──► Activation of amino acid + Charging of tRNA (ATP + Aminoacyl-tRNA Synthetase)
  2. INITIATION     ──► 30S/40S binds mRNA at Shine-Dalgarno / Kozak sequence; fMet-tRNA at P-site
  3. ELONGATION     ──► A-site entry ──► Peptidyl Transferase Peptide Bond ──► EF-G Translocation
  4. TERMINATION    ──► Release Factors (RF1/RF2) recognize Stop Codon ──► Polypeptide Released
conceptBreakdown.content:
### 8.1 Four Stages of Protein Synthesis
1. **Aminoacylation (tRNA Charging)**: Amino acid activated with $\text{ATP}$ to form aminoacyl-AMP, transferred to $3'\text{-OH}$ of tRNA catalyzed by **Aminoacyl-tRNA Synthetase** (consumes $\text{ATP} \rightarrow \text{AMP} + \text{PP}_i$).
2. **Initiation**:
   - Small ribosomal subunit ($30\text{S}/40\text{S}$) binds mRNA at the **Shine-Dalgarno sequence** ($5'\text{-AGGAGG-3'}$ in prokaryotes) or Kozak sequence in eukaryotes.
   - Initiator tRNA carrying $\text{fMet}$ binds directly into the **P-site (Peptidyl site)**.
   - Large subunit ($50\text{S}/60\text{S}$) docks to complete the initiation complex.
3. **Elongation & Peptidyl Transferase Ribozyme**:
   - **A-Site (Aminoacyl Site)** receives the next charged tRNA.
   - **Peptidyl Transferase** (a ribozyme: **$23\text{S}$ rRNA** in prokaryotes, **$28\text{S}$ rRNA** in eukaryotes) forms a peptide bond between the amino acid at the P-site and that at the A-site.
   - Translocation catalyzed by **EF-G (eEF-2)** shifts uncharged tRNA to the **E-site (Exit site)** for release.
4. **Termination**: Stop codons ($UAA, UAG, UGA$) bind **Release Factors (RF1, RF2)**, triggering hydrolysis of the ester bond and releasing the completed polypeptide.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Untranslated Regions (UTRs)
conceptBreakdown.title: Untranslated Regions (UTRs)
conceptBreakdown.content: UTRs are non-coding sequences present on mature mRNA located at both the 5'-end (before start codon) and 3'-end (after stop codon); they are essential for efficient ribosome binding and mRNA stability.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Polysomes (Polyribosomes)
conceptBreakdown.title: Polysomes (Polyribosomes)
conceptBreakdown.content: Multiple ribosomes translating a single mRNA molecule simultaneously form a Polysome (Polyribosome), producing multiple copies of the same polypeptide efficiently.
